title: Capacity fingerprint drift causing conservative autoscale decisions and reserved-pool shortfalls
creator: Samira Patel
description: Several customers experienced capacity shortfalls during short, high-intensity bursts on Dedicated pools. Traffic patterns showed rapid token bursts followed by normal traffic; our autoscaler failed to allocate burst headroom and reserved pools dropped below required capacity, triggering application coldstarts and degraded latencies for impacted tenants. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and a deployable fix to prevent recurrence.
reproduction_steps: Simulate a tenant workload with a 30s high QPS spike (3x baseline) followed by baseline traffic for 10 minutes
Observe autoscaler signals: short_term_load, moving_average_load, and burst_detector outputs on the affected region (us-west-2-dedicated-1)
Confirm that autoscaler increases target only after sustained load (>90s) and that reserved-pool reservations don't reflect the spike
Verify tenant experiences queued requests and instance coldstarts during the spike window
investigation_notes: Timeline: incident started 2026-03-01 14:07 UTC; first customer escalation 14:12 UTC; mitigation knob applied at 14:29 UTC
Telemetry: moving_average_load smoothing time-constant increased by 3x in last runtime release (runtime-1.39) due to refactor in telemetry aggregator
Observation: short_term burst detector was relying on the same smoothed metric, effectively silencing transient spikes below new smoothing horizon
Heap of related anomalies: KV cache warmups and per-tenant coldstart rate increased concurrently but root cause points to conservative scaling decisions
Affected tenants: 3 enterprise customers (vpn-health, courier.ai, studyhub) reported increased 95th/99th latency and queued requests; impact percent was 0.8% of total dedicated traffic for the region
root_cause: Telemetry aggregator refactor in runtime-1.39 unintentionally increased smoothing on the primary load signal used by burst detection. The burst detector consumed the smoothed metric instead of an un-smoothed short-window counter, suppressing transient spikes. Autoscaler safety logic treated the smoothed signal as canonical, delaying scale-ups and causing reserved-pool capacity shortfalls during brief bursts.
mitigation: Emergency: increased tenant-specific burst_limit_multiplier to 1.5 for affected pools (applied 2026-03-01 14:29 UTC) to allow temporary overcommit until fix deployed
Manual: temporarily provisioned two additional reserved instances to top-up pools for vpn-health and courier.ai
Operational: alerted on discrepancies between raw QPS percentiles (P95 short-window) and smoothed_load metric; added dashboard tile for immediate operator visibility
Customer comms: notified affected customers with RCA timeline and ETA for permanent fix via account teams
rollout_plan: Short-term: revert smoothing change for autoscaler input in a canary runtime (runtime-1.39-canary) and validate on synthetic burst tests (3/12)
Mid-term: implement separate short-window counter and dedicated burst-detector pipeline that uses percentile-based anomaly detection (P50/P95/P99 windows: 10s/30s/60s)
QA: run load replay using production traces for two days in canary; verify burst-detection FPR < 2% and recall > 95% for 30s spikes
Release: ship fix in runtime-1.40 with feature flag to toggle new detector; stage rollout region-by-region over 48 hours
Post-deploy: monitor reserved-pool headroom, burst hit rate, and customer latency for 72 hours with automated rollback if coldstart count > baseline + 10%
acceptance_criteria: New burst detector correctly triggers scale-ups for synthetic 30s bursts in canary with no more than 5s detection latency
No increase in false-positive scale-ups over a 24h production-equivalent trace replay (FPR < 2%)
Affected customers report no repeat regressions during follow-up window and receive final RCA
Change is behind a feature flag; operations runbook updated and dashboard alert added
